deep.reconstruction:
Authorship first: this sheet is not Riemann's own text. It is page 2 of Richard Dedekind's 'Erläuterungen' to Riemann's fragment on the limiting cases of the elliptic modular functions (fragment XXVIII). The previous page is headed 'Erläuterung zu dem vorstehenden Fragment', speaks of Riemann in the third person and mentions the printing. The commentary was published in Riemann's Werke (1876). This is where Dedekind introduces η and, on the following pages, the integer h, i.e. the later Dedekind sums.

Notation: 1^z = e^{2πiz}, ω = x+iy with y>0, q = 1^{ω/2} = e^{πiω}. The function is η(ω) = q^{1/12} ∏_{ν≥1}(1−q^{2ν}), the Dedekind eta function in modern notation (τ = ω).

(1) Logarithm. η has no zeros or poles in the simply connected upper half-plane. So every power η^s and log η are single-valued once fixed at one point. Normalization: log η(ω) − πiω/12 → 0 as y → ∞ (q → 0). This picks the branch log η = πiω/12 + Σ log(1−q^{2ν}) with principal logs near q = 0.

(2) Jacobi's product relations (cited as Fundamenta nova §36), rewritten via η:
(a) η(2ω) η(ω/2) η((1+ω)/2) = e^{πi/24} η(ω)^3.
(b) k^{1/4} = e^{πi/24} √2 η(2ω)/η((1+ω)/2), i.e. √2 q^{1/8} ∏(1+q^{2n})/(1+q^{2n−1}).
(c) k'^{1/4} = e^{πi/24} η(ω/2)/η((1+ω)/2), i.e. ∏(1−q^{2n−1})/(1+q^{2n−1}).
(d) √(2K/π) = e^{−πi/12} η((1+ω)/2)^2/η(ω), i.e. ∏(1−q^{2n})(1+q^{2n−1})^2 = θ_3(q).

My verification of (a): write η((1+ω)/2) = e^{πi/24} q^{1/24} ∏(1−(−q)^ν). Then ∏(1−q^ν)(1−(−q)^ν) = ∏(1−q^{2m})^3/∏(1−q^{4m}). Multiplying by η(2ω) gives e^{πi/24} q^{1/4} ∏(1−q^{2m})^3. (b)–(d) are checked the same way.

(3) Logarithmic forms. Using the normalization in (1), take logs:
- log η(2ω) + log η(ω/2) + log η((1+ω)/2) = πi/24 + 3 log η(ω).
- log k = log 4 + πi/6 + 4 log η(2ω) − 4 log η((1+ω)/2).
- log k' = πi/6 + 4 log η(ω/2) − 4 log η((1+ω)/2).
- log(2K/π) = −πi/6 + 4 log η((1+ω)/2) − 2 log η(ω).

The left-hand logs are defined (as in Fundamenta nova §40) as single-valued functions of ω such that log k − log 4 − πiω/2 = log k − log(4√q), log k' and log(2K/π) all tend to 0 as q → 0.

My check of the constants: as q → 0 the η-sides tend to
- (πi/4)ω + πi/24 versus (πi/4)ω, so the constant πi/24 is right;
- log 4 + πi/6 + (πi/2)ω − πi/6 = log 4 + πiω/2;
- πi/6 − πi/6 = 0;
- −πi/6 + πi/6 = 0.
So every constant is exactly the one forced by the normalizations.

(4) Programme stated at the end of the page. Combining this q → 0 behaviour with the first-order (unimodular) transformations of the θ-functions gives the behaviour as ω tends to a real rational value, i.e. as q tends to a root of unity. This is carried out on the next page through the transformation law of log η with the integer h.
errors: No mathematical errors: all four product identities and all additive constants (πi/24, πi/6, πi/6, −πi/6) are consistent with the stated normalizations.

Minor: the logarithmic identities follow from the product identities only up to multiples of 2πi. Fixing the constants needs the q→0 limits, which the text supplies implicitly ('zufolge der obigen Festsetzung'); the step is correct but only sketched.

results.modern_name: Dedekind eta function and its canonical logarithm
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind, 1876 (commentary in Riemann's Werke); the product itself goes back to Jacobi

results.modern_name: Jacobi product formulas / eta-quotient expressions for the modular lambda function and θ_3^2

results.what: Normalized logarithms of k, k', 2K/π as eta-log combinations, preparing the study of limits ω → rational
results.modern_name: Groundwork for the eta transformation law and Dedekind sums

deep.surprise_reason: The page is Dedekind's editorial commentary, not Riemann's own text. Its content is Jacobi's classical product identities in eta form plus a branch normalization. This is exactly the well-known published opening of Dedekind's 1876 'Erläuterungen', where the eta function is introduced. Nothing here is new or attributable to Riemann beyond what is already known.
